title: A major asymmetric ice trap in a planet-forming disk. III. First detection of dimethyl ether
question: What complex organic molecules and other species can be detected in the asymmetric ice trap of the IRS 48 planet-forming disk, and what are their column densities, abundance ratios, and chemical origins?

evidence.quote: We compare our results as summarised in Table 1 (100 K column) and Figure 3 with the observed abundances in other astronomical environments including the class 0 protostellar binary IRAS 16293 A and B (cite: jorgensen2018alma; manigand2020alma), the outbursting source V883 Ori (cite: lee2019ice), and the comet 67P (cite: drozdovskaya2019ingredients).

recipe.method: Image the line data with tclean in CASA using Briggs weighting (robust = 0.5), recentred to the star position with a Keplerian mask.

recipe.goal: Extract and stack disk-integrated spectra and make moment 0 and channel maps
recipe.method: Stack the cleaned images using GoFish over the whole azimuth of the disk to increase S/N, and create integrated intensity (moment 0) and channel maps of selected lines.
key_parameters: extraction over the whole azimuth of the disk

recipe.goal: Model LTE spectra to derive molecular column densities and upper limits
recipe.method: Convert flux densities to brightness temperature units and model stacked continuum-subtracted spectra in CASSIS assuming LTE, using CDMS and JPL spectroscopic databases, for transitions with E_up <= 400 K and A_ul >= 10^-5 s^-1.
key_parameters: T_ex = 100 K (and range 70 - 250 K for detected COMs; 40 K for NO)
assumptions: Source emitting area based on 5 sigma continuum emission (1.4 x 10^-11 sr) and beam dilution factor
12C/13C ratio of 60 for methanol isotopologue upper limit

answer_key.quantity: Methanol (CH3OH) column density (revised from weak lines, T_ex = 100 K)

evidence.quote: We use N() = $2\times10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ as a reference for comparisons.
We also derived a 3$\sigma$ upper limit for the column density of of $<$ 5.5 $\times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Strict upper limit on CH3OH column density (from 13CH3OH)

evidence.quote: This gives a strict upper limit on the column density of $\approx$ 3.3 $\times 10^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ assuming a / ratio of 60.

The / ratio in our disk is approximately 0.9 and this is consistent with what is observed in other sources across a full range of environments from star and disk formation to comets (cite: coletta2020evolutionary).

evidence.loc: Other line detections and upper limits
evidence.quote: From the CASSIS spectral analysis models, we derive a best-fit total column density for NO of at an excitation temperature of 40 K.
From the upper limit, we constrain this ratio to <10 %.
In IRS 48 we have an upper limit of $\approx$10%.

answer_key.quantity: Methanol D/H ratio upper limit (CH2DOH / CH3OH)

evidence.quote: This then gives an upper limit on the D/H of 10% and this is consistent with the ratios seen in protostellar cores, young low-mass stars, and comet 67P ($\approx$1%-10%, e.g. (cite: 2020A&A...639A..87V; 2021MNRAS.500.4901D)).

Some imaging/stacking parameters (calibration details, Keplerian mask parameters) require consulting companion papers (Ohashi et al. 2020, van der Marel et al. 2021a,b).
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA archival data (2017.1.00834.S, 2013.1.00100.S), well-defined spectral stacking and LTE modelling workflow using standard public tools (CASA, GoFish, CASSIS), and concrete numeric column density targets.
